messages:
incident-bot: PAGING: gpu-node-47 is reporting repeat Xid errors (Xid 13) and rising ECC correctable counts (>2k/hr). Observed container restarts on inference-pool-1. Severity: SEV2. @oncall please ack and escalate if needed
maya: acked. I'm oncall for infra today — joining bridge. First look: node shows nv-host-reset messages in dmesg, and kube OOM kills on model-worker pods.
raf: seeing similar on gpu-node-49. Telemetry shows a slow uptick starting ~20m ago after a large batch job. Could be thermal/driver or a model pattern triggering memory fragmentation.
samir: started customer impact check — 3 customers on hosted-api saw 5xx spikes, avg latency up 200ms for a subset of requests. Opening bridge and CC'ing support.
lina: @maya what's the kernel log look like? any Xid code details?
maya: tail of dmesg snippets: 
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, PID=23145; XidDetails: Graphics Exception on client 401
[ 12346.234567] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00:00: RmInitAdapter failed - device is lost
[ 12347.000123] EDAC MC0:   CE memory scrubbed - row eio
```
maya: ECC correctable counters are spiking. nv-smi shows GPU memory errors increasing. Node metrics: temp stable ~80C but ECC errors rising.
raf: I'm running `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-47` to list affected pods.
ops-bot: COMMAND: `kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-47 -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount` -> model-worker-7 (3), model-worker-9 (5), sidecar-logger (0)
raf: thanks bot. Those restarts line up with Xid timings.
samir: rolling action plan: 1) cordon node, 2) drain non-critical pods, 3) fallback heavy models to cpu-reserved hosts or smaller model variants, 4) create customer bridge if impact broad.
lina: agree. Also let's reduce batch sizes on the hosted-api edge routes hitting the affected models — throttling reduces memory pressure. @deploy-bot can you push a quick rate-limit config?
deploy-bot: Pushing config patch to rate-limit route 'gen-large' -> set max_batch_size=8, concurrency_limit=4. Deploy start -> canary 10%
maya: cordoning gpu-node-47 now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-47` -> succeeded. Starting drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` to get pods off.
ops-bot: Drain status: 6 pods evicted, 2 pods rescheduled to gpu-node-52 and gpu-node-53. model-worker-9 failed to reschedule due to resource requests; pending.
raf: manually scaled down the batch job that started earlier (`batch-inference-job-2026-03`). Reduced replicas from 40 -> 10. Watching error rate.
samir: Customer impact: hosted-api error rate for customer-*ids*: 5 customers saw intermittent 500s, grouped under heavy gen-large route. Notified CS to start proactive outreach.
customer-success: building a short customer message. Please confirm we have fallback routing in place before I push.
lina: fallback done: routes for gen-large now have fallback_model=smaller-gen-2 and a 5% traffic canary to smaller-gen-2, rest to main but rate-limited.
maya: telemetry update: ECC correctables slowed after cordon/drain and batch scale-down. Xid events still present but at lower rate. Kernel still logs occasional `RmInitAdapter failed`.
raf: can we capture nv-host logs and upload to S3 for postmortem? Command I ran: `sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "30 minutes ago" > /tmp/nvlogs.txt && gzip /tmp/nvlogs.txt && aws s3 cp /tmp/nvlogs.txt.gz s3://redwood-incidents/gpu-2659876543/`
maya: logs uploaded at s3://redwood-incidents/gpu-2659876543/nvlogs.txt.gz
samir: I'm creating an incident record with initial timeline + actions. Assigning to eng-runtime for deep dive. Ticket: INC-2026-0789.
lina: ops suggestion: mark node for soak and run memtest on GPU (driver tool) once it's out of production; we should also schedule a maintenance window to reseat GPUs if hardware team suggests.
maya: agreed. I'll put node into `maintenance` and open an internal hardware ticket.
ops-bot: NOTE: gpu-node-47 has NVidia BIOS version 470.94. For tracking: driver module nvidia 550.45.02.
raf: quick mitigation that helped: setting `--nvme-retry` (fabricated example) not applicable — ignore. Real mitigation was reducing batch size + draining node.
samir: customer bridge? Customer impact limited but growing earlier. Recommend opening a low-priority bridge for the 5 affected customers. @customer-success please invite.
customer-success: bridge started: bridge_link: https://meet.internal/bridge/INC-2026-0789. Invited 5 customers for post-incident notes.
maya: follow-ups: 1) leave node cordoned until hardware flake triage complete, 2) add telemetry alert for ECC correctables >200/hr per GPU, 3) re-evaluate driver version compatibility with BIOS, 4) run stress test with smaller-batch job to reproduce and capture core dumps.
lina: I'll add the alert to prometheus: `gpu_ecc_correctable_total{instance=~"gpu-node.*"} > 200` with 5m for 3/3 evals.
raf: will schedule a canary reroute for next 2 hours to ensure fallback is stable.
maya: handing off to day shift eng-runtime. I'm paged but moving to hardware ticket. If Xid resurges, escalate to SEV1 and unblock CS bridge.
samir: thanks all — keeping this thread open for updates. Current status: node cordoned & drained, customer bridge active, canary fallback + rate limits deployed, batch job scaled down. Monitoring. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy succeeded. Traffic shift to smaller-gen-2 10% stable for 6m.
ops-bot: Metric snapshot at 6m post-mitigation: ECC correctables per GPU: node-47 GPUs averaged 15/hr (down from 200+/hr). Pod restarts on drained node stopped.
customer-success: customers notified with preliminary ETA for full remediation after hardware triage.
raf: logging this thread into postmortems bucket and will link to INC-2026-0789.
maya: handing off fully — oncall to eng-runtime team now.
samir: last check-in in 30m then closing thread if stable.
